title: Emergency Provisions: Articles 352, 356, 360

endcard.line: Pictures: Beohar Rammanohar Sinha; David Castor (public domain); MohitSingh (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: Part Eighteen of the Constitution lets the Centre take extra powers in a crisis. There are three kinds of emergency.
Article three fifty-two: a national emergency, for war, external aggression or armed rebellion. The Centre can direct the states, and some rights can be suspended.
It has been used three times: in nineteen sixty-two, nineteen seventy-one, and from nineteen seventy-five to seventy-seven, on the ground of internal disturbance.

anim.title: The 44th Amendment, 1978
items: Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended

segments.say: After nineteen seventy-seven, the forty-fourth Amendment tightened it. 'Internal disturbance' became 'armed rebellion', the Cabinet must advise in writing, and the rights to life and liberty can never be suspended.

Article three fifty-six is President's Rule, when a state's government can't run as the Constitution says. In the Bommai case of nineteen ninety-four, the Supreme Court said it can be reviewed in court.

anim.title: Article 360: Financial Emergency
items: If India's financial stability is threatened
Centre can order cuts in salaries

segments.say: Article three sixty, a financial emergency, if India's financial stability is threatened. It has never been used.
For GS Two: three fifty-two, three fifty-six, three sixty. The forty-fourth Amendment's safeguards, and the Bommai judgment.

sources: Constitution of India, Part XVIII: Articles 352, 356, 358, 359 and 360
The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978: 'armed rebellion' replaces 'internal disturbance'; written advice of the Cabinet; Articles 20 and 21 not to be suspended under Article 359
S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) 3 SCC 1: proclamations under Article 356 are subject to judicial review
Lok Sabha Secretariat / NCERT Class 11, 'Indian Constitution at Work', ch. 7: proclamations of 1962, 1971 and 1975; Article 360 never invoked

quiz.q: Which amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'?
Which case made President's Rule reviewable by courts?
Which emergency has never been declared?

reviewNote: Facts were read against Part XVIII, the 44th Amendment Act and the Bommai judgment. Serious tone: stated plainly, no judgement on any government. Moving facts: none.
